title: A range from a setting
prompt: This program builds a range from a session setting and the `courses` table. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
n = int(spark.conf.get("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions"))
nums = spark.range(n, n * courses.count())
print(nums.count())
print(nums.columns + courses.columns[:1])
print(nums.sparkSession is courses.sparkSession)
hints: The shuffle setting is 4 in this environment, and `int` turns the text into a number.
Count the courses, then work out where the range starts and where it stops (the end is left out).
Both DataFrames were made through the session that's already running.
explanation: `n` is 4 and there are 4 courses, so the range runs from 4 up to (not including) 16: 12 rows. `columns` lists are plain Python lists, so `+` joins `['id']` and `['course_id']`. Every DataFrame here was made by the one running session, so `is` gives `True`.
